title: राजवंशीहरूको आफ्नो भाषाप्रतिको भाषिक अभिवृत्तिको विश्लेषण
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख ‘राजवंशीहरूको आफ्नो भाषाप्रतिको भाषिक अभिवृत्तिको विश्लेषण’ शीर्षकमा केन्द्रित छ । यस लेखमा समाजभाषावैज्ञानिक पद्धतिमा आधारित भएर राजवंशीहरूको भाषिक जीवन्तता, बहुभाषिक स्थिति, भाषिक प्रयोग र अभिवृत्तिको अवस्था के कस्तो रहेको छ ? भनी खोजी गर्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ । यसै क्रममा मिश्रित (गुणात्मक तथा परिमाणात्मक) अनुसन्धान ढाँचा अवलम्बन गरी राजवंशीभाषी वक्ता, उक्त भाषाका अध्येता, भाषा संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र संवद्र्धनमा सम्लग्न अभियान्ताहरूसँग प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाट गरी प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक दुवै स्रोतबाट तथ्याङ्कहरू सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । प्राथमिक तथ्याङ्क अन्तर्गत निर्मित प्रश्नावली, अन्तर्वार्ता र सम्बन्धित पक्षहरूसँग प्रत्यक्ष÷अप्रत्यक्ष रूपमा सहभागी भएर सङ्कलन गरिएको छ भने द्वितीयक स्रोत अन्तर्गत सम्बन्धित निकाय, तथ्याङ्क विभाग, विभिन्न पत्रपत्रिका, लेख रचनाहरू आदिबाट लिइएको छ । सङ्कलित तथ्याङ्कबाट विभिन्न थिम एवम् आशय निर्माण गरी प्राप्त नतिजालाई गुणात्मक र परिमाणात्क रूपमा मिश्रित ढाँचामा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । यो लेख भाषाका अध्येताहरूले राजवंशी भाषाका भाषिक जीवन्तता, भाषाप्रयोगको स्थिति र भाषिक अभिवृत्तिका बारेमा जानकारी लिन, आदिवासी तथा जनजातिहरूका भाषिक अवस्थाका बारेमा अध्ययन गरी भाषाका संरक्षण र संवद्र्धनका लागि योजना निर्माण गर्न, अदिवासी समुदायमा मातृभाषा शिक्षणका लागि पाठ्यक्रम निर्माण र पाठ्यपुस्तक लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउन, राज्यलाई मातृभाषाहरूका संरक्षण, संवद्र्धन र विकासका लागि भाषिक नीति र योजना निर्माण गर्न र यस विषयमा चासो राखी अध्ययन अनुसन्धान गर्न चाहने अनुसन्धानकर्ताहरूलाई समेत प्रत्यक्ष अप्रत्यक्ष रूपमा सहयोग पु¥याउनको लागि उपयोगी हुने छ ।
american_english:
This article is centered on the title 'An Analysis of the Linguistic Attitude of the Rajbanshi towards Their Own Language'.
In this article, an attempt has been made to investigate, on the basis of a sociolinguistic method, what the state of the linguistic vitality, multilingual situation, language use and attitude of the Rajbanshi is.
In this connection, adopting a mixed (qualitative and quantitative) research design, data have been collected from both primary and secondary sources by meeting directly with Rajbanshi-speaking speakers, scholars of that language, and activists engaged in the preservation and promotion of the language and culture.
Under primary data, collection has been done through a constructed questionnaire, interviews and direct/indirect participation with the concerned parties, while under secondary sources it has been drawn from the concerned bodies, the statistics department, various newspapers and magazines, articles and writings, and so on.
From the collected data, various themes and intents have been constructed, and the results obtained have been presented in a mixed format, qualitatively and quantitatively.
This article will be useful for language scholars to learn about the linguistic vitality of the Rajbanshi language, the state of language use and linguistic attitude; to study the linguistic situation of indigenous and tribal communities and formulate plans for the preservation and promotion of languages; to assist in curriculum development and textbook writing for mother-tongue instruction in indigenous communities; to help the state formulate language policy and plans for the preservation, promotion and development of mother tongues; and to indirectly assist researchers who wish to study and research this subject with interest.

informal_english: This article is about the analysis of how the Rajbanshi feel about their own language. In it, I've tried to find out, using a sociolinguistic approach, what the state of their language's vitality, their multilingual situation, their language use and their attitudes actually is. Along the way, I adopted a mixed (qualitative and quantitative) research design, gathering data from both primary and secondary sources by meeting directly with Rajbanshi speakers, scholars of the language, and activists involved in preserving and promoting the language and culture. Primary data came from a questionnaire I put together, interviews and direct/indirect participation with those concerned, while secondary sources included the relevant bodies, the statistics department, various newspapers and magazines, articles and writings, and the like. From the data collected, I built up various themes and intents, and presented the findings in a mixed qualitative and quantitative format. The article should be handy for language scholars wanting to learn about the vitality of the Rajbanshi language, language use and attitudes; for studying the linguistic situation of indigenous and tribal communities and drawing up plans to preserve and promote languages; for helping with curriculum development and textbook writing for mother-tongue teaching in indigenous communities; for helping the state shape language policy and plans for preserving, promoting and developing mother tongues; and for giving a hand to researchers keen to study this subject.
